newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CEPA has export plans for Allied Qld.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CEPA has export plans for Allied Qld.

text.p: Marsford Investments Pte Ltd, a unit of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA), said on Monday it planned to make Allied Queensland Coalfields Ltd a significant export earner if its takeover bid was successful.

Marsford also said it planned to increase production at the company's Wilkie Creek steaming coal mine in the Surat Basin and resolve longer term infrastructure problems with the state government to allow better access to port facilities.
It said its plans would require a capital commitment at some future date but did not specify the amount needed.

"Marsford will assist with the overseas marketing of the AQC's products and is hopeful that it will be able to acquire some medium to long term contracts from overseas which will make AQC into a significant export revenue earner for Queensland," the CEPA unit said in its takeover document.

Marsford earlier on Monday launched a 70 cent per share bid for Allied Queensland, valuing the Brisbane-based miner at A$19.33 million. It already has a 17.8 percent stake and will pay a total of A$16.054 million for the remaining shares if the bid is successful. Its bid topped by 10 cents per share the offer by Centennial Coal Ltd launched last Friday.
Clyde Petroleum Plc, which has a controlling stake of 43.4 percent in Allied Queensland, told Reuters it would sell to Marsford in the absence of a higher offer.
Clyde gained its stake in Allied Queensland earlier this year with its takeover of Australian petroleum producer and explorer Crusader Ltd.
Shares in Allied Queensland ended six cents higher at 72 cents, a 12 month high on wishful speculation by some investors that a bidding war may be about to begin, brokers said.
CEPA is the power generation division of Gordon Wu's Hopewell Holdings Ltd. --Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
